capitals.name: Maghas (site disputed; Arkhyz is one proposal)
capitals.note: Al-Mas'udi (930s): Maghas 'was the capital of the Alans', though their king moved between residences. Proposed sites: Arkhyz in Karachay-Cherkessia (three 10th-century churches), North Ossetia, Il'ichevskoye Gorodische in Krasnodar Krai, Ingushetia. The coordinates are Arkhyz.

correction.text: the plain and foothills of the North Caucasus from the Laba to the Argun, up to the Darial Gorge

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row; the page gives no area. 'Before the Mongol invasion, the Alans lived in the territory from the Laba River to the Argun'; 'the Alan kingdom stretched from Daghestan to Abkhazia' (al-Mas'udi, 10th century); the western edge at the Kuban headwaters and the eastern at the Darial Gorge. The core is the five republics of the central North Caucasus; Daghestan and Abkhazia are the tenth-century claim of one author and are not drawn.

region.text: the plain and foothills of the North Caucasus from the Laba to the Argun, up to the Darial Gorge

ledger.note: Late 9th century: Alania frees itself from the Khazars. 'In the late 9th century, Alania became independent from the Khazars'; infobox 'Independence from the Khazars: late 9th century'. The page gives no year; 880 is the researcher's pick.
November-December 1239: the Mongols besiege Maghas. 'the siege of Maghas, which began in November or December 1239' (the Maghas page: the 11th lunar month of 1239, 27 November to 26 December).
February 1240: Maghas falls. The siege 'ended in the 2nd lunar month of 1240 (i.e. 6-24 February)' (Yuanshi, via the Maghas page); infobox 'Fall of Maghas: 1240'.

region.text: the plain and foothills of the North Caucasus from the Laba to the Argun, up to the Darial Gorge

ledger.note: 1240: the Alan kingdom ends. Infobox 'Fall of Maghas: 1240', 'succeeded by the Mongol Empire'; the Alans page: 'Most Alans submitted to the Mongol Empire in 1239-1277'.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Alania
wars.outcome: The Mongols under Batu stormed and destroyed Maghas; the siege ran from late 1239 to February 1240; most Alans submitted to the Mongol Empire in 1239-1277.

certainty.note: Only the river limits (Laba, Argun, Darial Gorge) are given; the capital's site is itself disputed.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks Alania; its 'Alans' row 414-438 is the Iberian Alans). The ia-01-d notes proposed 723-969 for Alania from the Khazars page; the Alania page gives no 8th-century founding (only a buffer-state role in the Byzantine-Arab and Khazar-Arab wars of the 8th century) and dates independence to the late 9th century, so the dossier starts in 880. Between the Alans of the Pontic steppe (375, the sarmatians dossier) and 880 the Alans of the Caucasus 'fell under the overlordship of the Khazar Khaganate' (page, undated) and are not drawn. The Khazaria dossier keeps the north Caucasus piedmont in its shape to 964, so the Alania shape overlaps Khazaria 880-964: a gap-filler should decide which draws it. Territory beyond the core (Daghestan to Abkhazia) is Mas'udi's tenth-century claim. Timur's 1395 defeat of the Golden Horde on the Terek is outside the dossier. No area, no ruler list. Gazetteer names used (five North Caucasus republics) resolve.
